correctness.rationale: An adjacent-label conjugation involution proves the previously known conditional descent expectation. Marking a two-cycle gives the exact covariance factorization. The positive-coefficient derangement recurrence produces a mixture distribution and an inductively valid stochastic sandwich, with strictness from the one-long-cycle event. An analogous two-marking argument establishes the opposite unconditioned sign. All boundary cases and quantifiers are covered analytically. The standalone exact-rational checker performs 3,295 assertions, including exhaustive enumeration through n=8 and distributional checks through n=35; no finite range is mistaken for the infinite proof.

Eriksen–Freij–Wästlund (2008), §§2 and 7: derangement descent-set enumerators and correlation of being a derangement with descent events; no Ewens cycle-count function appears.
Da Silva–Jamshidpey–Tavaré (2020), §§2 and Appendix A: Ewens cycle distributions, factorial moments, and ordered-cycle-length monotonicity; no descent statistic is analyzed.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Broader joint generating functions encode the joint law and can in principle recover the covariance at each fixed n. They do not by themselves provide the claimed stochastic-order proof or an all-n strict positivity assertion, so no inspected result has been shown to imply the complete sign theorem directly. The original 1993 full text was not inspected and remains a qualified coverage risk.

Da Silva–Jamshidpey–Tavaré (2020), formula (9), counts derangements by cycle count but not jointly by ordinary descents.

originality.rationale: A direct comparison with full accessible primary sources finds that Fulman (1998) supplies the class-conditional first moment, Bóna (2006) the derangement cycle-count polynomials, Eriksen–Freij–Wästlund (2008) descent-set enumeration under conditioning, and da Silva–Jamshidpey–Tavaré (2020) Ewens derangement cycle marginals and cycle-length monotonicity. None of the inspected source statements gives the all-theta all-size increasing-transform cycle-count/ordinary-descent covariance sign or the sandwich. A general generating function of Gessel–Reutenauer (1993) provides broader information about joint distributions and thus poses a real unresolved historical-priority risk, but its cited theorem alone does not state or prove an all-size positivity inequality.
residual_risks: The 1993 Gessel–Reutenauer original joint-generating-function paper was not available for full-text comparison; a hidden specialization could anticipate the sign statement.
Fulman (1998) original full text was not inspected, although the used conditional-mean formula is explicitly acknowledged as old.
A mathematically equivalent sign result in specialized later derangement–descent literature not returned by the searches remains possible.

value.rationale: The exact sign reversal between uniform permutations and fixed-point-free permutations is a natural dependence question, not an arbitrary parameter slice. The all-theta and arbitrary strictly increasing function scope significantly strengthens a single covariance value.
